risk_register.description: Integrating symbolic planning formalisms with LLM-based reasoning may prove more difficult than anticipated, particularly in achieving real-time performance for the planning engine.
risk_register.mitigation: Adopt a modular architecture with well-defined interfaces between symbolic and neural components. Implement fallback modes where the LLM-only planner operates when symbolic integration introduces unacceptable latency. Begin integration testing from M6, not M18. [Affects: WP2 (Neuro-Symbolic Planning and Reasoning Engine)]

risk_register.description: The tri-store memory architecture may not scale to the interaction lengths required by demonstrators (hundreds of steps) without unacceptable latency or storage costs.
risk_register.mitigation: Design the memory controller with configurable retention policies from the start. Conduct scalability stress-testing on synthetic long-horizon tasks from M9. Implement tiered storage with fast/approximate retrieval for working memory and precise/slower retrieval for episodic memory. [Affects: WP3 (Adaptive Memory Architecture)]

risk_register.description: Formal convergence proofs may be achievable only for restricted task classes, not for the full generality of real-world multi-agent scenarios encountered in demonstrators.
risk_register.mitigation: Classify task types early (M3–M6) by coordination complexity. Prioritise convergence proofs for the most common demonstrator task patterns. Use probabilistic convergence bounds for task classes where deterministic proofs are infeasible. [Affects: WP4 (Decentralised Multi-Agent Coordination)]

risk_register.description: Access to de-identified clinical datasets may be delayed by ethics review processes or restricted in scope, reducing the clinical validation power of the healthcare demonstrator.
risk_register.mitigation: Submit ethics applications in M1 (pre-project preparation already initiated). Use publicly available clinical datasets (MIMIC-IV, eICU) for initial development and intermediate evaluation. Design the demonstrator with a data abstraction layer that can switch between data sources. [Affects: WP5 (Healthcare Demonstrator — Clinical Decision Support)]

risk_register.description: Operational factory access for the manufacturing demonstrator may be interrupted by production schedules, equipment maintenance, or external disruptions.
risk_register.mitigation: Secure a formal access agreement with factory partners before project start. Schedule the 3-month validation period with buffer windows. Develop a high-fidelity digital twin of the pilot factory that can substitute for physical access during development phases. [Affects: WP6 (Manufacturing Demonstrator — Process Optimisation)]

risk_register.description: ELI operational data may be subject to commercial confidentiality constraints that restrict the scope or publishability of transfer demonstrator results.
risk_register.mitigation: Negotiate data access and publication terms in the consortium agreement. Design the demonstrator with an anonymisation layer that enables publication of performance metrics without exposing proprietary data. Supplement with public logistics benchmarks. [Affects: WP7 (Logistics Transfer Demonstrator — Cross-Sector Generalisation)]

risk_register.description: The fast pace of LLM development may produce new foundation models during the project that significantly change the baseline capabilities, requiring re-evaluation of MAESTRO's value proposition.
risk_register.mitigation: Design all MAESTRO components with model-agnostic interfaces that can integrate new LLMs without architectural changes. Conduct annual baseline re-evaluation (M12, M24, M36) against latest models. MAESTRO's value lies in the architecture (planning, memory, coordination) not in any specific LLM. [Affects: WP2 (Neuro-Symbolic Planning and Reasoning Engine), WP3 (Adaptive Memory Architecture), WP4 (Decentralised Multi-Agent Coordination), WP8 (Integration, Evaluation and Benchmarking)]

risk_register.description: Regulatory requirements under the EU AI Act for high-risk AI systems (particularly the healthcare demonstrator) may impose compliance obligations that require additional development effort.
risk_register.mitigation: Monitor EU AI Act implementing regulations throughout the project. Design auditability and transparency mechanisms from the start (audit trails, decision explanations). Engage with AI regulatory sandboxes where available. [Affects: WP5 (Healthcare Demonstrator — Clinical Decision Support), WP6 (Manufacturing Demonstrator — Process Optimisation), WP8 (Integration, Evaluation and Benchmarking)]

risk_register.description: A key partner may reduce commitment or a principal investigator may depart during the project, creating capability gaps.
risk_register.mitigation: Ensure each pillar has at least 2 partners with relevant expertise. Include deputy PI appointments for each WP lead. Consortium agreement includes commitment clauses and transition procedures. [Affects: WP1 (Project Management and Coordination)]

risk_register.description: The independently developed planning, memory, coordination, and tool orchestration modules may not integrate cleanly into a unified framework, requiring significant re-engineering.
risk_register.mitigation: Define shared data representations, API contracts, tool registry schemas, and integration interfaces in M1–M3 (WP8 early deliverable). Conduct integration checkpoints every 6 months. Assign BAL as integration engineer across all three pillars and the tool orchestration layer. [Affects: WP2 (Neuro-Symbolic Planning and Reasoning Engine), WP3 (Adaptive Memory Architecture), WP4 (Decentralised Multi-Agent Coordination), WP8 (Integration, Evaluation and Benchmarking)]

risk_register.description: The diversity of external APIs across three demonstrator domains (HL7 FHIR in healthcare, OPC-UA in manufacturing, logistics tracking/customs APIs) may require more adapter development effort than planned, delaying tool orchestration layer readiness.
risk_register.mitigation: Define a minimal common adapter interface in M1–M3. Prioritise adapters for the most critical APIs per demonstrator. Use existing open-source connector libraries where available rather than building from scratch. [Affects: WP2 (Neuro-Symbolic Planning and Reasoning Engine), WP3 (Adaptive Memory Architecture), WP5 (Healthcare Demonstrator — Clinical Decision Support), WP6 (Manufacturing Demonstrator — Process Optimisation), WP7 (Logistics Transfer Demonstrator — Cross-Sector Generalisation), WP8 (Integration, Evaluation and Benchmarking)]

issues.description: The project develops and deploys AI-based autonomous agent systems (MAESTRO framework) capable of autonomous planning, tool use, and decision-making. Ethical concerns related to human rights and values — including transparency, accountability, and human oversight — arise from the deployment of AI agents in high-stakes domains (healthcare clinical decision support, manufacturing process control).

ethics_assessment.self_assessment_statement: The project requires a full ethics self-assessment as part of the application, consistent with the Tier 1 rule that applicants must complete an ethics self-assessment and that projects with ethics issues may undergo ethics review with ethics requirements potentially becoming contractual obligations (docs/tier1_normative_framework/extracted/implementation_constraints.json: ethics_self_assessment_required; source: wp-15-general-annexes_horizon-2026-2027_en.pdf p.16; programme-guide_horizon_en.pdf pp.25-28). The Tier 3 compliance_profile.json records ethics_review_required: true as a compliance flag derived during call binding; no Tier 2B extracted source path in docs/tier2b_topic_and_call_sources/extracted/ cites ethics review as a topic-specific mandate for this call — this flag is treated as a Tier 3 derivative compliance indicator consistent with the Tier 1 default rule. Ethics issues identified include: AI system ethics (Category 8) arising from autonomous agent deployment in healthcare and manufacturing; human participants and personal health data processing (Categories 2 and 4) in the healthcare demonstrator (WP5); civil focus compliance (Declaration 7). The ethics self-assessment table (application form section A.4) must be completed as an essential part of the proposal. Ethics appraisal will cover compliance with ethical principles, relevant legislation, proportionality of methods, and applicant awareness of ethical and social impacts per Tier 1 rule (implementation_constraints.json: ethics_appraisal_summary). The Tier 3 compliance_profile.json records gender_plan_required: true as a compliance flag derived during call binding; no Tier 2B extracted source path cites gender equality plan as a topic-specific mandate for this call — this flag is treated as a Tier 3 derivative compliance indicator consistent with the Tier 1 rule that public bodies, research organisations, and higher education establishments must have a gender equality plan at grant signature (implementation_constraints.json: gender_equality_plan_eligibility; source: wp-15-general-annexes_horizon-2026-2027_en.pdf pp.18-19). Integration of the gender dimension in research and innovation content follows the Tier 1 default rule that it is mandatory unless the topic explicitly states non-relevance. No Tier 2B exemption source is currently cited in this Phase 6 artifact; Phase 8 drafting must either add the relevant Tier 2B topic-source reference or keep the claim framed as pending call-specific confirmation.
